source_checks.finding: Section 'Change brightness manually' says: 'To adjust display brightness, select the Network icon on the right side of the taskbar' and then 'move the Brightness slider to adjust the brightness.' It also says 'You might not see the Brightness slider on desktop PCs that have an external monitor,' and 'To change the brightness on an external monitor, use the buttons on it.' The page lists Windows 11 and Windows 10, so the Windows 11 applicability holds.
Same section says: 'Alternatively, you can adjust the display brightness from Settings > System > Display.' Supports the second route for Windows 11.

required_actions.action: Raise screen brightness through the taskbar Network icon and Brightness slider
Offer the Settings > System > Display route
Tell external monitor users to use the monitor buttons

source_checks.finding: Section 'Adjust brightness in Control Center' confirms the iPhone X or later swipe down from the top-right corner, and iPhone 8 or earlier swipe up from the bottom edge, and 'Drag the brightness bar up or down to adjust the brightness.' This is an iPhone-only route and does not apply to a computer, so it is correctly unused in the clarify question.

Section 'Change brightness manually' confirms the Windows Network icon and Brightness slider route. It is a Windows route, so it is relevant only if the user's computer is a Windows PC. It does not cover Macs.

required_actions.action: Find out which device the user means
Do not offer phone options when the user said the device is a computer

findings: The user wrote 'It's on my computer.' The routed question is 'Is your device an iPhone, an Android phone, or a Windows 11 PC?', which offers phone options the user did not indicate, so it does not respect what the user said.

The routed question leaves out Mac. A computer can be a Mac, and the Windows 11 route and the Mac route give different steps, so the omission means the one question does not separate the real options.
correction_required: Replace the routed question and target with: 'Is your computer a Windows 11 PC or a Mac?' Update the route basis to say that the user named a computer, so the choice is between the computer types. If a Mac answer must lead to steps later, the candidate needs a Mac source in its set; the clarify question itself does not need one.

source_checks.finding: Section 'Adaptive brightness' says: 'To automatically fit your screen's brightness to the light around you, turn on Adaptive brightness,' and 'This option is on by default.' The page covers Pixel phones, so the Android (Pixel phone) applicability holds. It is one of the device-specific routes that the clarify question separates.

Section 'Change brightness manually' confirms the Windows 11 Network icon route, which is a different device route from the Pixel adaptive setting. It supports the need to ask which device before answering.

required_actions.action: Find out which device the screen is on

source_checks.finding: Section 'Adaptive brightness' says: 'To automatically fit your screen's brightness to the light around you, turn on Adaptive brightness,' 'This option is on by default,' and that on Pixel 4 and later Pixel phones adaptive brightness 'can temporarily brighten your screen above the normal maximum' in extremely bright ambient lighting, 'like direct sunlight.' A narrower re-check confirmed the switch sits in Display & touch settings. The Pixel 4 and later condition is stated on the page.

Section 'Brightness level' confirms 'Open your phone's Settings app,' 'Tap Display & touch,' and 'To set your screen's brightness, tap Brightness level and move the slider.' The user already did this step, and the target correctly does not repeat it.

required_actions.action: Check that Adaptive brightness is turned on
Explain that Pixel 4 and later can brighten above the normal maximum in direct sunlight
Do not repeat the Brightness level slider step the user already completed

source_checks.finding: Section 'If a temperature warning screen appears' says: 'If your device exceeds a certain temperature threshold, it will present a temperature warning screen similar to this,' then steps 'Turn off your device,' 'Move your device to a cooler environment (away from direct sunlight),' and 'Allow your device to cool down.' It also says 'An iPhone showing this message might still be able to make emergency calls.' The page covers iOS and iPadOS devices, so the iPhone applicability holds.

required_actions.action: Move the iPhone out of direct sunlight to a cooler place
Mention that the warning phone may still make emergency calls

findings: The target says 'Yes. Turn off your iPhone first, then follow these steps on your iPhone:' and then lists '1. Turn off your device.' The same action appears twice, which is repetition the user does not need.
correction_required: Remove the duplicate turn-off step. Use: 'Yes. Turn off your iPhone first. Then:' followed by '1. Move your device to a cooler environment (away from direct sunlight).' and '2. Allow your device to cool down.'
